finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches an attacker-supplied URL after a weak suffix check. endswith("example.com") has no dot boundary, so hosts like evilexample.com pass and the server requests internal or metadata addresses that the attacker's DNS points to.
finding.source: Query parameter 'url' at mirror.py:11 (async def mirror(url: str)), supplied by any unauthenticated network client.
finding.sink: Outbound HTTP GET c.get(url) at mirror.py:16 using httpx.AsyncClient, made from the server's network position.

trace.note: url taken from the query string with no sanitisation
only check: host.endswith("example.com") with no dot boundary; attacker-registered evilexample.com passes
default AsyncClient, no follow_redirects setting and no IP-range restriction
c.get(url) requests the original unvalidated URL string, not the validated host
only len(r.text) is returned, so the response is a length-only oracle

finding.guards_checked: Hostname suffix check at mirror.py:13 (bypassable by evilexample.com; ALLOWED_SUFFIX=".example.com" at line 7 is defined but unused, suggesting the intended dot-boundary check was lost). No scheme restriction, but httpx only handles http/https so file:// is not reachable. No private/loopback/link-local IP blocking. No redirect controls (httpx default is believed to be no redirects, not verified against the installed version). /ping at lines 20-24 is hardcoded and not a finding. Possible urlparse vs httpx host-parser differential for crafted authority strings (backslash, @) is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the suffix test at mirror.py:13 (`host.endswith("example.com")`), which has no dot boundary and does not close the finding. ALLOWED_SUFFIX at mirror.py:7 is unused. No IP-range, scheme, or exact-hostname check exists anywhere in mirror.py.
verdict.reason: The `url` query parameter (mirror.py:11) reaches `c.get(url)` at mirror.py:16 after only `host.endswith("example.com")` at mirror.py:13, so an attacker-registered `evilexample.com` passes and the server fetches whatever its DNS resolves to, including internal or metadata addresses; every trace line matches the file, and the response is exposed as a length oracle at mirror.py:17.
